pairs: non potui vobis loqui quasi spiritualibus,
I was not able to speak to you as if to those who are spiritual,
but rather as if to those who are carnal.
For you are like infants in Christ.
I gave you milk to drink,
For you were not yet able.
And indeed, even now, you are not able;
Cum enim sit inter vos zelus,
And since there is still envy
and are you not walking according to man?
Ego quidem sum Pauli; alius autem:
I am of Paul,” while another says,
“I am of Apollo,” are you not men?
We are only the ministers of him in whom you have believed,
just as the Lord has granted to each of you.
Itaque neque qui plantat est aliquid,
And so, neither he who plants, nor he who waters,
but only God, who provides the growth.
But each shall receive his proper reward,
According to the grace of God,
which has been given to me,
I have laid the foundation like a wise architect.
So then, let each one be careful how he builds upon it.
Fundamentum enim aliud nemo potest ponere præter id quod positum est,
For no one is able to lay any other foundation, in place of that which has been laid,
Si quis autem superædificat super fundamentum hoc,
But if anyone builds upon this foundation,
each one’s work shall be made manifest.
For the day of the Lord shall declare it,
because it will be revealed by fire.
And this fire will test each one’s work,
as to what kind it is.
Si cujus opus manserit quod superædificavit,
If anyone’s work, which he has built upon it, remains,
then he will receive a reward.
If anyone’s work is burned up,
but he himself will still be saved,
Do you not know that you are the Temple of God,
et Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis?
and that the Spirit of God lives within you?
Si quis autem templum Dei violaverit,
But if anyone violates the Temple of God,
For the Temple of God is holy,
si quis videtur inter vos sapiens esse in hoc sæculo,
If anyone among you seems to be wise in this age, let him become foolish,
so that he may be truly wise.
Sapientia enim hujus mundi, stultitia est apud Deum.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God.
And so it has been written:
“I will catch the wise in their own astuteness.”
Dominus novit cogitationes sapientium quoniam vanæ sunt.
“The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain.”
And so, let no one glory in men.
